stimulus: Recent studies of sediment in the North Atlantic’s deep waters expose likely cyclical patterns in the history of Earth’s climate. The rock fragments in these sediments are too huge to have been transported there by ocean currents; they must have arrived at their current locations by traveling in large icebergs that floated long distances from their point of origin before melting. Geologist Gerard Bond noticed that some of the sediment grains were stained with iron oxide, evidence that they originated in locales where glaciers had overrun outcrops of red sandstone. Bond’s detailed analysis of deep-water sediment cores showed changes in the mix of sediment sources as time goes by: the proportion of these red-stained grains fluctuated back and forth from lows of 5 percent to highs of about 17 percent, and these fluctuations occurred in an almost regular 1,500-year cycle. Bond hypothesized that the alternating cycles might be evidence of changes in ocean-water circulation and thereby in Earth’s climate. He knew that the sources of the red-stained grains were usually closer to the North Pole than were the places yielding a high proportion of “clean ” grains. At certain times, ob viously, more icebergs from the Arctic Ocean in the far north were traveling south well into the North Atlantic before melting and shedding their sediment. Ocean waters are continually moving, and water temperatur e is both a reason and an effect of this movement. As water cools, it becomes denser and sinks to the ocean’s bottom. During some periods, the bottom layer of the world’s oceans comes from cold, dense water sinking in the far North Atlan tic. This leads to the warm surface waters of the Gulf Stream to be pulled northward. Bond re cognized that during such pe riods, the influx of these warm surface waters into northern regions could result in a large proportion of the icebergs that bear red grains to melt before traveling very far into the North Atlantic. But now and then the ocean’s dynamic changes, and waters from the Gulf Stream do not travel northward in this way. During these periods, surface waters in the North Atlantic would usually be colder, permitting icebergs bearing red-stained grains to travel farther south in the North Atlantic before melting and depositing their sediment. The initiation of the so-called Little Ice Age (1300-1860), which followed the Medieval Warm Period of the eighth through tenth centuries, may stand for the most recent time that the ocean’s dynamic changed in this way. If unremitting climate-history studies support Bond’s hypothesis of 1,500-year cycles, scientists may set up a major natural rhythm in Earth’s temperatures that could then be estimated into the future. Because the midpoint of the Medieval Warm Period was about 850, an extension of Bond’s cycles would place the midpoint of the next warm interval in the twenty-fourth century.
prompt: According to the passage, which of the following is true of the rock fragments contained in the sediments studied by Bond?

options.text: The majority of them are composed of red sandstone.

They were carried by icebergs to their present location.
Most of them were carried to their present location during a warm period in Earth’s climatic history.
They are unlikely to have been carried to their present location during the Little Ice Age.

explanation: 正確答案為 C（They were carried by icebergs to their present location.）。首段說岩石碎片 too huge to have been transported there by ocean currents；they must have arrived…by traveling in large icebergs，故選 C。A 文中說紅色顆粒比例只有 5% 至 17%；E 方向相反，小冰期正是冰山南移時期。

stimulus: Recent studies of sediment in the North Atlantic’s deep waters expose likely cyclical patterns in the history of Earth’s climate. The rock fragments in these sediments are too huge to have been transported there by ocean currents; they must have arrived at their current locations by traveling in large icebergs that floated long distances from their point of origin before melting. Geologist Gerard Bond noticed that some of the sediment grains were stained with iron oxide, evidence that they originated in locales where glaciers had overrun outcrops of red sandstone. Bond’s detailed analysis of deep-water sediment cores showed changes in the mix of sediment sources as time goes by: the proportion of these red-stained grains fluctuated back and forth from lows of 5 percent to highs of about 17 percent, and these fluctuations occurred in an almost regular 1,500-year cycle. Bond hypothesized that the alternating cycles might be evidence of changes in ocean-water circulation and thereby in Earth’s climate. He knew that the sources of the red-stained grains were usually closer to the North Pole than were the places yielding a high proportion of “clean ” grains. At certain times, ob viously, more icebergs from the Arctic Ocean in the far north were traveling south well into the North Atlantic before melting and shedding their sediment. Ocean waters are continually moving, and water temperatur e is both a reason and an effect of this movement. As water cools, it becomes denser and sinks to the ocean’s bottom. During some periods, the bottom layer of the world’s oceans comes from cold, dense water sinking in the far North Atlan tic. This leads to the warm surface waters of the Gulf Stream to be pulled northward. Bond re cognized that during such pe riods, the influx of these warm surface waters into northern regions could result in a large proportion of the icebergs that bear red grains to melt before traveling very far into the North Atlantic. But now and then the ocean’s dynamic changes, and waters from the Gulf Stream do not travel northward in this way. During these periods, surface waters in the North Atlantic would usually be colder, permitting icebergs bearing red-stained grains to travel farther south in the North Atlantic before melting and depositing their sediment. The initiation of the so-called Little Ice Age (1300-1860), which followed the Medieval Warm Period of the eighth through tenth centuries, may stand for the most recent time that the ocean’s dynamic changed in this way. If unremitting climate-history studies support Bond’s hypothesis of 1,500-year cycles, scientists may set up a major natural rhythm in Earth’s temperatures that could then be estimated into the future. Because the midpoint of the Medieval Warm Period was about 850, an extension of Bond’s cycles would place the midpoint of the next warm interval in the twenty-fourth century.
prompt: In the final paragraph of the passage , the author is concerned primarily with

options.text: answering a question about Earth’s climatic history
pointing out a potential flaw in Bond’s hypothesis
suggesting a new focus for the study of ocean sediments
tracing the general history of Earth’s climate
discussing possible implications of Bond’s hypothesis

explanation: 正確答案為 E（discussing possible implications of Bond’s hypothesis）。末段說若研究支持 Bond 的 1,500 年週期，scientists may set up a major natural rhythm…estimated into the future，並推算下次溫暖期中點在二十四世紀，即討論其假說的可能意涵。B 文中未指出缺陷；C 並未提出新研究方向。

stimulus: In Raisin in the Sun , Lorraine Hansberry does not refuse integration or the economic and moral promise of the American dream; rather, she remains loyal to this dream while looking, practically, at its partial realization. Once we realize this dual vision, we can accept the play’s ironic nuances as deliberate social commentaries by Hansberry rather than as the “unintentional” irony that Bigsby ascr ibe to the work. Indeed, a curi ously persistent refusal to credit Hansberry with a capacity for deliberately irony has caused some critics to interpret the play’s thematic conflicts as mere confusion, contradiction, or eclectic ism. Isaacs, for instance, cannot easily reconcile Hansberry’s intense concern for her race with her ideal of human reconciliation. But the play’s complicated view of Black self-esteem and human solidarity as compatible is no more “contradictory” than Du Bois’ famous, well-considered ideal of ethnic self-awareness coexisting with human unity, or Fanon’s emphasis on an ideal internationalism that also accommodates national identities and roles.
prompt: The author of the passage would probably consider which of the following judgments to be most similar to the reasoning of the critics mentioned in line 5?

options.text: The world is certainly flat; therefore, the person proposing to sail around it is unquestionably foolhardy.
Radioactivity cannot be directly perceived; therefore, a scientist could not possibly control it in a laboratory.
The painter of this picture could not intend it to be funny; therefore, its humor must result from a lack of skill.
Traditional social mores are beneficial to cultur e; therefore, anyone who deviates from them acts destructively.
Filmmakers who produce documentaries deal exclus ively with facts; therefore, a filmmaker who reinterprets particular events is misleading us.

explanation: 正確答案為 C（The painter of this picture could not intend it to be funny; therefore, its humor must result from a lack…）。這些評論者因為先認定 Hansberry 沒有「capacity for deliberate irony」，便把劇中衝突解讀為「mere confusion」。C 同樣先認定畫家不可能有意幽默，再把幽默歸因於技巧不足，推理結構最相似。A 只是從錯誤前提推論，未涉及否認作者意圖。

stimulus: While the influence of British magazines in shaping public opinion precedes the nineteenth century, it was during the 1800s that mass distribution became feasible and an explosion in periodical readership occurred, immensely growing magazines’ opinion-shaping powers. The role of mag azines as arbiters of ninete enth-century taste is seen in their descriptions of the London Theater. The magazines coincided some legitimacy with East End working-class theaters that reflected the format of the prevalent West End theaters serving middle- and upper-class audiences. However, the magazines also portrayed mu sic halls—which contended for patronage with all theaters—as places where crass entertainment corrupted spectators’ taste and morals. Finally, they suggested that popular demand for substandard fare created a market unamiable to higher expressions of dramatic art.
prompt: The author of the passage attributes the influence of British periodicals in shaping public opinion in the nineteenth century in part to

options.text: a growing public interest in reading opinion pieces
an increase in the relative number of readers from the middle and upper classes
changes in the way in which magazines were distributed
magazines’ increased coverage of theater and popular entertainment
changes in magazine format that attracted a wider readership

explanation: 正確答案為 C（changes in the way in which magazines were distributed）。首句說十九世紀 mass distribution became feasible，期刊讀者大增，因而大幅提升雜誌塑造輿論的力量，即影響力部分源於發行方式的改變。B 錯，文中沒說中上階層讀者比例增加；E 的版面改變文中未提。

stimulus: Historians credit repeated locust invasions in the nineteenth century with reshaping United States agriculture west of the Mississippi River. Admonished by government entomologists, farmers began to diversify. Wheat had come to almost monopolize the region, but it was especially vulnerable to the locusts. In 1873, just before the locusts’ most withering offensive, almost two-thirds of Minnesota farmland was producing wheat; by the invasions’ last year, that fraction had dropped to less than one-sixth. Farmers learned that peas and beans were far less vulnerable to the insects, and corn was a more robust grain than wheat. Besides planting alternative crops, many farmers turned to dairy and beef production. Despite pastures were often dama ged by the locusts, these lands were nearly always left in better shape than the crops were.
prompt: According to the passage, before the recommendations by the government entomologists, which of the following was true about farming west of theMississippi River?

options.text: Farmers focused primarily on growing wheat.
Peas and beans had not yet been planted in the region.
A relatively small portion of farmland was devoted to crops other than wheat.

explanation: 正確答案為 A（Farmers focused primarily on growing wheat.）、C（A relatively small portion of farmland was devoted to crops other than wheat.）。A 對：wheat had come to almost monopolize the region，1873 年明尼蘇達近三分之二農地種小麥。C 對：其他作物僅占小部分。B 錯，文中沒說豌豆與豆類尚未種植。

stimulus: Objectively, of course, the diverse ecosystems that ma intain life on the planet pro ceed independently of human agency, just as they operated before the hectic ascendancy of Homo sapiens. But it is also true that it is hard to think of a single such system that has not, for better or worse, been virtually modified by human culture. Nor is this simply the work of the industrial centuries. It has been happening since the days of ancient Mesopotamia. It is coetaneous with the origins of writing, and has occurred over all our social existence. And it is this irreversibly modified world, from the polar caps to the equatorial forests, that is all the nature we have.
prompt: It can be inferred from the passage that the author would agree with which of the following statements?

options.text: Over tie, the impact of human culture on the natural world has been largely benign.
It is a mistake to think that the natural world contains many areas of pristine wilderness.
The only substantial effects that human agency has had on ecosystems have been inadvertent.

explanation: 正確答案為 B（It is a mistake to think that the natural world contains many areas of pristine wilderness.）。作者說「很難想到任何一個生態系統未被人類文化改造」，且這個被改造的世界就是我們僅有的自然，可推知他認為未受干擾的荒野幾乎不存在。A 錯，文中說改造是「for better or worse」，未判定為良性；C 的「無意」文中未提。

stimulus: The most believable justification for higher taxes on au tomobile fuel is that fuel consumption diminishes the environment and thus increases the costs of traffic cong estion. But the fact that burning fuel generates these “negative externalities” does not indicate that no tax on fuel could ever be too high. Economics is accurate about the tax that should, in principle, be levied to cope with negative externalities: the tax on a liter of fuel should equals the harm resulted from using a liter of fuel. If the tax is more than that, its costs (including the inconvenience to those who would rather have used their cars) will exceed its benefits (including any reduction in congestion and pollution).
prompt: In the last sentence, “exceed” most closely means

options.text: outstrip
magnify
delimit
offset
supplant

explanation: 正確答案為 A（outstrip）。末句說若稅額過高，成本（包括不便）會「exceed」效益（包括減少壅塞與污染），意思是超過、勝過，對應 outstrip。D 的 offset（抵銷）是指兩者相當，並不表示超過。

stimulus: Frederick Douglass was undeniably the most renowned African American of the nineteenth century; in fact when he died in 1895 he was among the most distinguished public figures in the United States. In his study of Douglass’ career as a main figure in the movement to abolish slav ery and as a spokesman for Black rights, Waldo Martin has stirred controversy by stating that Douglass also deserves a eminent place in the intellectual history of the United States because he exemplified so many strands of nineteenth-century thought: romanticism, idealism, individualism, liberal humanism, and an unshakable belief in progress. However this very argument offers ammunition for those who declare that most of Douglass’ ideas, being so representative of their time, are now obsolete. Douglass’ farsight of the future as a melting pot in which all racial and et hnic differences would blend into “a composite American nationality” appears from the pluralist perspective of many present-day intellectuals to be not only utopian but even wrongheaded. Yet there is a core aspect of Douglass’ thought that seems not in the least bit dated or irrelevant to current concerns. He has no opponent in the history of the nineteenth-century United States as an persistent and effective critic of the doctrine of in nate racial inequality. He not only attacked racist ideas in his speeches and writings, but he dedicated his whole career and all his achievements as living proof that racists were incorrect in their belief that one race could be intrinsically superior to another. While Martin stresses Douglass’ antiracist egalitarianism, he does not sufficiently illustrate how this aspect of Douglass’ thought fits in with his espousal of the liberal Vic- torian attitudes that many current intellectuals view to be naïve and outdated. The fact is that Douglass was capt ivated by these democratic-capitalist ideals of his time because they could be used to raid slavery and the doctrine of White supremacy. His favorite rhetorical strategy was to expose the hypocrisy of those who, while professing at tachment to the ideals of democracy and equality of opportunity, condoned slavery and racial discrimination. It would have been absurd indeed if he had not embraced liberal idealism, for it verified its worth for the cause of racial equality during the national crisis that eventually led to emancipation and citizenship for African Americans. These points may seem apparent, but had Martin given them more attention, his analysis might have composed a more effectual rebuttal to those critics who threw out Douglass’ ideology as a debris of the past. If one accepts the proposition that Douglass’ deepest commitment was to Black equality and that he utilized the liberal ideals of his time as weapons in the battle for that cause, then it is difficult to fault him for capturing the best weapons at hand.
prompt: The passage as a whole can best be described as doing which of the following?

options.text: Explaining Douglass’ emergence as a major figure in the movement to abolish slavery
Tracing the origins of Douglass’ thought in nineteenth-century romanticism, idealism, and liberal humanism
Analyzing Douglass’ speeches and writings from a modern, pluralist perspective
Criticizing Martin for failing to stress the contradiction between Douglass’ principles and the liberal Victorian attitudes of his day
Formulating a response to those who consider Douglass’ political philosophy to be archaic and irrelevant

explanation: 正確答案為 E（Formulating a response to those who consider Douglass’ political philosophy to be archaic and irrelevant）。作者指出有人認為 Douglass 思想「now obsolete」，接著說明其反種族主義核心並不過時，並解釋他擁抱自由主義理想是用作武器，以回應這些批評者。選項「批評 Martin 未強調矛盾」錯，作者認為兩者並不矛盾，只怪 Martin 沒說明其如何契合。

stimulus: What triggers a helix in nature to emerge with either a dextral (“right-handed,” or clockwise) twist or a sinistral (“left-handed,” or counterclockwise) twist is one of the most captivating puzzles in the science of form. Most spiral-shaped snail species are dominantly dextral. But at one time, handedness (twist direction of the shell) was equally presented within some snail species that have become predominantly dextral or, in a few species, predominantly sinistral. What mechanisms influence handedness and keep left-handedness scarce? It would seem impossible that evolution should discriminate against sinistral snails if sinistral and dextral snails are actual mirror images, for any disadvantage that a sinistral twist in itself could confer on its possessor is almost incredible. But left- and right-handed snails are not actually true mirror images of one another. Their shapes are remarkably different. Sinistral scarcity might, then, be a consequence of possible disadvantages conferred by these other concomitant structural features. Furthermore, perhaps left- and right-handed snails cannot mate with each other, having inappropriate twist di rections. Presumably an individual of the rarer form would have relevant difficulty in searching a mate of the same hand, thus keeping the rare form rare or generating geographically separated right- and left-handed populations. However this evolutionary mechanism blending di ssymmetry, anatomy, and chance does not supply an adequate explanation of why right-handedness should have become prevailing. It does not explain, for instance, why the uncommon unions between snails of opposing hands produce fewer offspring of the rarer than the commoner form in species where each parent contributes equally to handedness. Nor does it illustrate why, in a species where one parent influences handedness, a brood is not exclusively right- or left-handed when the offspring would have the same genetic predisposition. In the European pond snail Lymnaea peregra, a remarkably dextral species whose handedness is maternally determined, a brood might be anticipated to be exclusively right- or left-handed—and this often happens. However, some broods owns a few snails of the opposing hand, and in dominantly sinistral broods, the incidence of dextrality is astonishingly high. Here, the evolutionary theory must defer to a theory according to an explicit developmental mechanism that can support either right- or left-handedness. In the case of Lymnaea peregra, studies reveal that a dextral gene is expressed during egg formation; i.e., before egg fertilization, the gene produces a protein, discovered in the cytoplasm of the egg, that controls the pattern of cell division and thus handedness. In experiments, an injection of cytoplasm from dextral eggs shifts the pattern of sinistral eggs, but an injection from sinistral eggs does not affect dextral eggs. One illustration for the differing effects is that all Lymnaea peregra eggs start left-handed but most switch to being right-handed. Therefore the path to a solution to the puzzle of handedness in all snails seems to be as twisted as the helix itself.
prompt: Which of the following would serve as an example of “concomitant structural features” (line 13) that might disadvantage a snail of the rarer form?

options.text: shell and body that are an exact mirror image of a snail of the commoner form
A smaller population of the snails of the rarer form
A chip or fracture in the shell caused by an object falling on it
A pattern on the shell that better camouflages it
A smaller shell opening that restricts mobility and ingestion relative to that of a snail of the commoner form

explanation: 正確答案為 E（A smaller shell opening that restricts mobility and ingestion relative to that of a snail of the commoner form）。文中說左右旋蝸牛「not actually true mirror images」，形狀明顯不同，稀少可能源於這些伴隨的構造特徵帶來的劣勢；較小的殼口限制移動與進食，正是構造上的劣勢。B 族群較小並非構造；C 外力造成的破損並非先天構造。

stimulus: In the early twentieth century, the id ea that pianists should be musician-scholars whose playing reflected the way composers needed their music to sound alternated the notion that pianists should be virtuosos whose performances delighted audiences with emotional daring and flashy displays of technique. One significant figure to appear in the period, though a harpsichordist rather than a pianist, was Wanda Landowska (1879–1959). She explained how the keyboard works of Baroque composers such as Bach, Handel, Scarlatti, an d Couperin possibly sounded in their own times. It would be an error to view Landowska a cla ssicist, however. She had been born in an age of Romantic playing predominated by Liszt, Leschetizky, and their pu pils. Therefore she grew up with and was affected by certain Romantic traditions of performance, whatever the stringency of her musical scholarship; Landowska realized how to hold audiences breathless, and when she gave recitals, they replied with deathlike silence and rapt attention. Her playing was Romantic, but it was at least as close in spirit to the style of playing intended by composers of the Baroque (1600–1750) and Classical (1750–1830) ages, as have been the more demanding but less emotionally resonant interpretations of most harpsichordists since Landowska. She hd a marvelous quality of touch, a seemingly autonomous left hand; no artist in her generation could clarify with such adroitness the polyphonic writing of the Baroque masters. And none could make their music so spring to life. Her achievements were the consequence of a lifetime of scholarship, truly remarkable physical gifts, and resilient rhythm, all mixed with extraordinary judgment ab out when not to hold the printed note sacrosanct. Of course, building such judgment required substantial experience and imagination. She was a genius at underscoring the dramatic and emotional content of a piece, and to do so, she took liberties, all kinds of liberties, while notwithstanding conserving the integrity of a composer’s score. In brief, her whole musical approach was Romantic: extensively personal, full of light and shade, never pedantic. Because of Landowska, Bach’s music (initially compos ed for the harpsichord) now sounded inappropriately thick when played on the piano. One by one, pianists ped playing Bach’s music as adjusted for the piano by Liszt or by Tausig. Then they steadily ped performing any kind of Baroque music on the piano, even Scarlatti’s. The piano repertoire, it started to be felt, was extensive enough without returning to transcriptions of Baroque music previously written for the harpsichord—and piano perfo rmances of Bach and Scarlatti were, in spite of the obvious similarities between the harpsichord and the piano, transcriptions, no matter how faithfully the original notes were played. In harmony with this type of purism came an emphasis on studying composers’ manuscript notations, a comparatively new field of musicology that is booming even today.

Performances emphasizing showy displays of technique that compromise the integrity of a composer’s original score.

explanation: 正確答案為 E（Performances emphasizing showy displays of technique that compromise the integrity of a composer’s original score.）。文中說她雖「took liberties」，卻仍「conserving the integrity of a composer’s score」，可見她拒絕犧牲樂譜原意的炫技。A 錯，她的演奏充滿情感；D 正是作者讚揚她的判斷力。

stimulus: Mary Barton, particularly in its early chapters, is a moving response to the suffering of the industrial worker in the England of the 1840’s. What is most impressive about the book is the intense and painstaking effort made by the author, Elizabeth Gaskell, to convey the experience of ev eryday life in working-class homes. Her method is partly documentary in nature: the novel includes such features as a carefully annotated reproduction of dialect, the exact details of food prices in an account of a tea party, an itemized descript ion of the furniture of the Bartons’ living room, and a transcription (again annotated) of the ballad “The Oldham Weaver.” The interest of this record is considerable, even though the method has a slightly distancing effect. As a member of the middle class, Gaskell could hardly help approaching working- class life as an outside observer and a reporter, and the reader of the novel is always conscious of this fact. But there is genuine imaginative re-creation in her accounts of the walk in Green Heys Fields, of tea at the Bartons’ house, and of John Barton and his friend’s discovery of the starving family in the cellar in the chapter “Poverty and Death.” Indeed, for a similarly convincing re-creation of such families’ emotions and responses (which are more crucial than the material details on which the mere reporter is apt to concentrate), the English novel had to wait 60 years for the early writing of D. H. Lawrence. If Gaskell never quite conveys the sense of full participation that would completely authenticate this aspect of Mary Barton , she still brings to these scenes an intuitive recognition of feelings that has its own sufficient conviction. The chapter “Old Alice’s History” br illiantly dramatizes the situation of that early generation of workers brought from the villages and the countryside to the urban industrial centers. The account of Job Legh, the weaver and naturalist who is devoted to the study of biology, vividly embodies one kind of response to an urban industrial environment: an affinity for living things that hardens, by its very contrast with its environment, into a kind of crankiness. The early chapters—about factory workers walking out in spring into Green Heys Fields; about Alice Wilson, remembering in her cellar the twig-gathering for brooms in the native village that she will never again see; about Job Legh, intent on his impaled insects—capture the characteristic responses of a generation to the new and crushing experience of industrialism. The other early chapters eloquently portray the development of the instinctive cooperation with each other that was already becoming an important tradition among workers.

Experimental prose style based on working-class dialect

stimulus: The work of English writer Aphra Be hn (1640–1689) changed significantly during the 1680s, as she turned from writing plays to writing prose narratives. Based on literary critic Rachel Carnell, most scholars regard this change as principally motivated by financial considerations: making a living by writing for the theatre became tougher in the 1680s, so Behn tried various other types of prose genr es in the hope of finding another lucrative medium. In reality, a long epistolary scandal novel that she wrote in the mid-1680s sold quite well. Yet, as Carnell notes, Behn did not replicate this approach in her other prose works; instead, she turned to writing shorter, more serious novels, even if only about half of these were published duri ng her lifetime. Carnell contends that Behn, whose stage productions are initially comedies, may have turned to an emerging literary form, the novel, in a conscious attempt to criticize, and overturn for her own ends, the conventions and ideology of a well-established form of her day, the dramatic tragedy. Carnell acknowledges that Behn admired the skill of su ch contemporary writers of dramatic tragedy as John Dryden, and that Behn’s own comic stage productions revealed the same partisanship for the reigning Stuart monarchy that characterized most of the politically oriented dramatic tragedies of her day. Nevertheless, Carnell contends that Behn argued with the way in which these writers and plays defined the nature of tragedy. As prescribed by Dryden, tragedy was supposed to concern a heroic man who is a public figure and who experiences a fall that arouses pity from the audience. Carnell indicates that Behn’s tragic novels focus instead on the plight of little-known women and the private world of the household; even in her few novels fe aturing male protagonists, Behn insists on the significance of the crimes these othe rwise heroic figures commit in the domestic sphere. In addition, in accordance with Carnell, Behn questioned the view spread by monarchist dramatic tragedies such as Dryden’s: that the envisioned “public” political ideal—passive obedience to the nation’s king—should to be mirrored in the private sphere, with family members totally obedient to a male head of household. Carnell sees Behn’s novels not only as rejecting the model of patriarchal and hierarchical family order, but also as warning that insisting on such a parallel can result in real tragedy befalling the member s of the domestic sphere. In accordance with Carnell, Behn’s choice of literary form emphasizes the distinctions between her own approach to crafting a tragic story and that taken in the dramatic tragedies, with their artificial distinction between the public and private spheres. Behn’s novels engage in the political dialogue of her era by demonstrating that the good of the nation essentially encompasses more than the good of the public figures who rule it.
prompt: The passage is primarily concerned with

options.text: tracing how Behn’s view of the nature of tragedy changed over time
explaining one author’s view of Behn’s contribution to the development of an emerging literary form
differentiating between the early and the late literary works of Behn
contrasting the approaches to tragedy taken by Behn and by Dryden
presenting one scholar’s explanation for a major development in Behn’s literary career

explanation: 正確答案為 E（presenting one scholar’s explanation for a major development in Behn’s literary career）。全文介紹 Carnell 對 Behn 由劇本轉向小說的解釋：並非主要出於財務考量，而是有意 criticize, and overturn…the conventions and ideology of…dramatic tragedy，即一位學者對其生涯重大轉變的解釋。D 只是論證的一部分；B 重點錯在文學形式的發展。

stimulus: Over the decades, biologists have proposed two major pathways by which sexual selection may have shaped the development of male birdsong. For one thing, male competition and intrasexual selection generate relatively brief, simple songs used primarily in territorial behavior. For another, female choice and intersexual selection produce longer, more complex songs utilized mainly in mate attraction; similar to such visual decoration as the peacock’s tail, elaborate vocal characteristics raise the male’s possibil ities of being selected as a mate, and he thus earns more reproductive success than his less ostentatious rivals. The two pathways are not mutually exclusive, and we can expect to find examples that mirror their interaction. Teasing them apart has been a significant challenge to evolutionary biologists. Early research established the role of intrasexual selection. In a set of experiments in the field, males replied violently to recorded songs by displaying territorial beha vior near the speakers. The breakthrough for research into intersexual selection came in the invention of a new technique for studying female response in the laboratory. When female cowbirds living in isolation in sound-proof chambers were exposed to recordings of male song, they replied by exhibiting mating behavior. By measuring th e responses, researchers were capable to confirm what special features of the song were most significant. In further experiments on song sparrows, researchers discovered that when exposed to a single song type repeated several times or to a repertoire of distinctive song types, females replied more to the latter. The beauty of the experimental design is that it effectively rules out confusing variables; acoustic isolation ensures that the female can reply only to the song structure itself. If intersexual selection operates as theorized, males wi th more complex songs should not only attract females more readily but should also obtain greater reproductive success. At first, however, researchers doing fieldwork with song sparrows discovered no connection between larger repertoires and early mating, which has been revealed to be one indicator of reproductive success; further, common measures of male quality utilized to forecast reproductive success, such as weight, size, age, and territory, also failed to connect with song complexity. The confirmation researchers had been seeking was eventually acquired in studies involving two categories of warblers. Unlike the song sparrow, which repeats one of its several song types in bouts before shifting to another, the warbler constantly composes much longer and more variable songs without repetition. For the first time, researchers discovered an important correlation between re pertoire size and early mating, and they further found that repertoire size had a more significant effect than any other measure of male quality on the number of young produced. The evidence reveals that warblers apply their ex traordinarily elaborate songs mainly to attract females, apparently confirming the effect of intersexual selection on the evolution of birdsong.

stimulus: Over the decades, biologists have proposed two major pathways by which sexual selection may have shaped the development of male birdsong. For one thing, male competition and intrasexual selection generate relatively brief, simple songs used primarily in territorial behavior. For another, female choice and intersexual selection produce longer, more complex songs utilized mainly in mate attraction; similar to such visual decoration as the peacock’s tail, elaborate vocal characteristics raise the male’s possibil ities of being selected as a mate, and he thus earns more reproductive success than his less ostentatious rivals. The two pathways are not mutually exclusive, and we can expect to find examples that mirror their interaction. Teasing them apart has been a significant challenge to evolutionary biologists. Early research established the role of intrasexual selection. In a set of experiments in the field, males replied violently to recorded songs by displaying territorial beha vior near the speakers. The breakthrough for research into intersexual selection came in the invention of a new technique for studying female response in the laboratory. When female cowbirds living in isolation in sound-proof chambers were exposed to recordings of male song, they replied by exhibiting mating behavior. By measuring th e responses, researchers were capable to confirm what special features of the song were most significant. In further experiments on song sparrows, researchers discovered that when exposed to a single song type repeated several times or to a repertoire of distinctive song types, females replied more to the latter. The beauty of the experimental design is that it effectively rules out confusing variables; acoustic isolation ensures that the female can reply only to the song structure itself. If intersexual selection operates as theorized, males wi th more complex songs should not only attract females more readily but should also obtain greater reproductive success. At first, however, researchers doing fieldwork with song sparrows discovered no connection between larger repertoires and early mating, which has been revealed to be one indicator of reproductive success; further, common measures of male quality utilized to forecast reproductive success, such as weight, size, age, and territory, also failed to connect with song complexity. The confirmation researchers had been seeking was eventually acquired in studies involving two categories of warblers. Unlike the song sparrow, which repeats one of its several song types in bouts before shifting to another, the warbler constantly composes much longer and more variable songs without repetition. For the first time, researchers discovered an important correlation between re pertoire size and early mating, and they further found that repertoire size had a more significant effect than any other measure of male quality on the number of young produced. The evidence reveals that warblers apply their ex traordinarily elaborate songs mainly to attract females, apparently confirming the effect of intersexual selection on the evolution of birdsong.

draw a distinction between competing theories of intersexual selection
give an example of a feature that may have evolved through intersexual selection by female choice
refute a commonly held assumption about the role of song in mate attraction

explanation: 正確答案為 D（give an example of a feature that may have evolved through intersexual selection by female choice）。作者在說明 female choice 與 intersexual selection 產生複雜歌聲時，以孔雀尾巴這種視覺裝飾作類比，說明精緻特徵能提高被選為配偶的機會。選項「說明兩種途徑都重要」錯，孔雀尾巴只對應雌性選擇這一條途徑。

stimulus: Nineteenth-century architect Eugène-Emmanuel Viollet-le-Duc argued that Paris’s Notre-Dame cathedral, built initially in the late twelfth century, was supported from the very beginning by a system of flying buttresses — a series of exterior arches (flyers) and their supports (buttresses) — which permitted the construction of taller vaulted buildings with slimmer walls and interior supports than had been possible formerly. Nevertheless other commentators insist that Notre-Dame did not have flying bu ttresses until the thirteenth or fourteenth century, when they were added to update the building aesthetica lly and amend its structural flaws. Even though post-twelfth-century modifications and renovations complicate efforts to resolve this argument — all pre-fifteenth-century flyers have been substituted, and th e buttresses have been rebuilt and/or resurfaced — it is nevertheless possible to tell that both the nave and the choi r, the church’s two main parts, have always had flying buttresses. It is clear, now that nineteenth-century paint and plaster have been removed, that the nave’s lower buttresses date from the twelfth century. In addition, the choir’s lower flyers have chevron (zigzag) decoration. Chevron decoration, which was characteristic of the second half of the twelfth century and was out of favor by the fourteenth century, is thoroughly absent from modifications to the building that can be dated with confidence to the thirteenth century.

explaining why evidence relevant to a controversy has been overlooked

explanation: 正確答案為 C（arguing in support of one side in a controversy）。作者先介紹 Viollet-le-Duc 與其他評論者的爭議，再用「it is nevertheless possible to tell that both the nave and the choir … have always had flying buttresses」，並以十二世紀扶壁及 chevron 裝飾佐證，支持 Viollet-le-Duc 一方。B 的困難只是讓步內容。

stimulus: Music critics have consistently defined James P. Johnson as a great early jazz pianist, originator of the 1920s Harlem “stride” style, and a significant blues and jazz composer. Moreover, however, Johnson was an innovator in classical music, composing symphonic music that incorporated American, and especially African American, traditions. Such a blend of musical elements was not completely new: by 1924 both Milhaud and Gershwin had composed classical works that incorporated elements of ja zz. Johnson, a serious musician more veteran than most classical composers with jazz, blues, spirituals, and popul ar music, was peculiarly suited to expand Milhaud’s and Gershwin’s experiments. In 1927 he accomplished his first large-scale work, the blues- and jazz-inspired Yamekraw, which contained borrowings from spirituals and Johnson’s own popular songs. Yamekraw, premiered triumphantly in Carnegie Hall, was main achievement for Johnson, becoming his most frequently performed extended work. It demonstrated vividly the possibility of assimilating contemporary popular music into the symphonic tradition.
prompt: Which of the following best describes the organization of the passage?

options.text: A historical overview is presented, and a particular phenomenon is noted and analyzed.
A popular belief is challenged, and a rival interpretation is presented and supported.
A common viewpoint is presented and modified, and the modification is supported.
An observation is made and rejected, and evidence for that rejection is presented.
A common claim is investigated, and an alternative outlook is analyzed and criticized.

explanation: 正確答案為 C（A common viewpoint is presented and modified, and the modification is supported.）。首句先陳述常見看法：評論家視 Johnson 為爵士鋼琴家與作曲家；接著以「Moreover, however」補充修正，說他也是古典音樂的創新者；最後以《Yamekraw》支持這項修正。B 錯在原觀點並沒有被推翻。

stimulus: The reduction in responsiveness that follows continuous stimulation (adaptation) is usual to all sensory systems, including olfaction. With continued exposure to chronically present ambient odors, individuals’ perception of odor intensity is highly decreased. In addi tion, these perceptual changes can be meaningful and everlasting. It is generally reported that following extended absences from the odorous environment, reexposure may still fail to elicit perception at the initial intensity. Most research on olfactory adaptation examines correspondingly ephemeral changes in stimulus detection or perceived intensity—rarely superior several hours and often less—but because olfactory adaptation can be produced with correspondingly short exposures, these durations are sufficient for investigating many parameters of the phenomenon. Nevertheless, exposures to odors in natura l environments often occur over far longer periods, and the resulting adaptations may differ qualitatively from short-term olfactory adaptation. For instance, studies show that even concise periods of odorant stimulation produce ephemeral reductions in receptors in the olfactory epithelium, a process termed “receptor fatigue.” Prolon ged odor stimulation, however, could generate more long-lasting reductions in response, possibly involving structures higher in the central nervous system pathway.
prompt: According to the passage, the phenomenon of olfactory adaptation may cause individuals who are reexposed to an odorous environment after an extended absence to

options.text: experience a heightened perception of the odor
perceive the odor as being less intense than it was upon first exposure
return to their original level of perception of the odor
exhibit a decreased tolerance for the odorous environment
experience the phenomenon of adaptation in other sensory systems

explanation: 正確答案為 B（perceive the odor as being less intense than it was upon first…）。文中說 following extended absences from the odorous environment, reexposure may still fail to elicit perception at the initial intensity，即再度接觸時感覺氣味不如最初強烈，選 B。C 方向相反；A 的 heightened 與適應的減弱相反。

stimulus: Historian F. W. Maitland discovered that legal documents are the best—in fact, often the only—available evidence about the economic and social history of a designated period. Why, then, has it taken so long for historians to focus systematically on the civil (noncriminal) law of early modern (sixteenth- to eighteenth-century) England? Maitland gave one reason: the subject requests researchers to “master an extremely formal system of pleading and procedure.” Yet the complexities that confront those who would study such materials are not totally different from those recently conquered by historians of criminal law in England during the same period. Another probable explanation for historians’ neglect of the subject is their widespread assumption that most people in early modern England hardly had any contact with civil law. If that were true, the history of legal matters would be of little relevance to general historical scholarship. But latest research suggests that civil litigation during the period involved artisans, merchants, professi onals, shopkeepers, and farmers, and not merely a narrow, propertied, male elite. stimulus: In 1996, scientists resulted in an experimental flood of the Colorado River by relieving water from Glen Canyon Dam above the Grand Canyon. Because an unintentional flood in 1983 had lowered the river’s introduced population of nonnative trout, biologists were anxious that the experimental flood would flush many fish, native and nonnative, downstream. To find out, biologists cast nets in the river. The nets captivated a few more trout than they would have without the flood but did not include substantial flushing of native fish, whose ancestors had, after all, survived many larger natural floods. The biologists speculated that the native species (and most of the trout) must have rapidly retreated to safeguarded areas along the riverbank.
prompt: Which of the following, if true, would make the information presented in the passage compatible with the experimental flood’s in fact having caused considerable flushing of native fish?

options.text: Many of the native fish are too small to have been captivated by the nets.
There had been an increase from normal levels in the native fish population prior to the flood.
The native fish in the Colorado are much stronger swimmers than taxonomically similar fish in other rivers in the region.
The unintentional flood of 1983 had not influenced the river’s trout population as much as was initially thought.
The experimental flood elevated the water level much less than a typical natural flood would have.

explanation: 正確答案為 A（Many of the native fish are too small to have been captivated by the nets.）。生物學家的結論依據撒網結果：網中沒有大量原生魚。若許多原生魚 too small to have been captivated by the nets，牠們即使被沖走也不會被網到，資訊便與大量沖刷相容。E 只說明洪水較小，反而更支持沒有沖刷；D 與原生魚無關。

stimulus: Since the 1970s, archaeological sites in China's Yangtze River region have generated evidence of sophisticated rice-farming societies prior to signs of rice agriculture el sewhere in East Asia by a thousand years. Before this evidence was discovered, it had generally been inferred that rice farming originated farther to the south. This scenario was based both on the geographic range of wild or free-living rice, which was not considered to broaden as far north as the Yangtze, and on archaeological records of very early domestic rice from Southeast Asia and India (now known to be not so old as first reported). Advocates of the southern-origin theory claimed that early rice-farming societies along the Yangtze were already greatly advanced and that evidence for the first stage of rice cultivation is lacking. They argue that the first hunter-gatherers to initiate rice agriculture must have done so in this southern zone, within the evident present-day geographic range of wild rice. Yet while most strands of wild rice reported in a 1984 survey were centralized to the south of the Yangtze drainage, two northern strange populations were also detected in provinces along the middle and lower Yangtze, evidence that the Yangtze wetlands may fall within both the present-day and the historical geographic ranges of rice's wild ancestor.
prompt: Which of the following, if true, would most clearly diminish the conclusion that the author makes on the basis of the 1984 survey?

options.text: Areas south of the Yangtze basin currently have less wild-rice habitat than they once did.
Surveys since 1984 have shown wild rice populations along the upper Yangtze as well as along the middle and lower Yangtze.
The populations of wild rice along the Yangtze symbolize strains of wild rice that migrated to the north relatively recently.
Early rice-farming societies along the Yangtze were not as highly developed as archaeologists once thought.
In East Asia, the historical geographic range of wild rice was more extensive than the present-day geographic range is.

explanation: 正確答案為 C（The populations of wild rice along the Yangtze symbolize strains of wild rice that migrated to the north relatively recently.）。作者根據 1984 年調查推論揚子江濕地可能同時位於野生稻的現今與「historical」分布範圍。若那些族群是近期才往北遷移，就只能證明現今分布，無法支持歷史分布，結論因而被削弱。B、E 反而支持作者。

stimulus: The nearly circular orbits of planets in our solar system caused scientists to anticipate that planets around other stars would also occupy in circular orbits. stimulus: Despite winning several prestigious literary awards of the day, when it first appeared, Alice Walker’s The Color Purple generated critical unease over puzzling aspects of its compositions. In what, as one reviewer put it, was “clearly intended to be a realistic n ovel,” many reviewers perceived violations of the conventions of the realistic novel form, pointing out variously that late in the book, the narrator protagonist Celie and her friends are propelled toward a happy ending with more velocity than credibility, that the letters from Nettie to her sister Celie intrude into the middle of the main action with little motivation or warrant, and that the device of Celie’s letters to God is especially unrealistic inasmuch as it forgoes the concretizing details that traditionally have given the epistolary novel (that is, a novel composed of letters) its peculiar verisimilitude: the ruses to enable mailing letters, the cache, and especially the letters received in return. Indeed, the violations of realistic convention are so flagrant that they might well call into question whether The Color Purple is indeed intended to be a realistic novel, especia lly since there are indications that at least some of those aspects of the novel regarded by viewers as puzzlin g may constitutes its links to modes of writing other than Anglo-European nineteenth-century realism. For example, Henry Louis Gates, Jr., has recently located the letters to God within an African American tradition deriving from sl ave narrative, a tradition in which the act of writing is linked to a powerful deity who “speaks” through scripture a nd bestows literacy as an act of grace. For Gates, the concern with finding a voice, which he sees as the defini ng feature of African Ameri can literature, links Celie’s letters with certain narrative aspects of Zora Neale Hurston’s 1937 novel Their Eyes Were Watching God, the acknowledged predecessor of The Color Purple. Gates’s paradigm suggests how misleading it may be to assume that mainstream realist criteria are appropriate for evaluating The Color Purple . But in his preoccupation with voice as a primary element unifying both the speaking subject and the text as a whole Gates does not elucidate many of the more conventional structural features of Walker’s novel. For instance, while the letters from Nettie clearly illustrate Nettie’s acquisition of her own voice, Gates’s focus on “voice” sheds little light on the place that these letters occupy in the narrative or on why the plot takes this sudden jump into geographically and culturally removed surroundings. What is needed is an evaluative paradigm that, rather than obscuring such startling structural features (which may actually be explicitly intended to undermine traditional Anglo-European novelistic conventions), confronts them, thus illuminating the deliberately provocative ways in which The Color Purple departs from the traditional models to which it has been compared.
prompt: According to the passage, an evaluative paradigm that confronts the startling structural features of The Color Purple would accomplish which of the following?

options.text: It would adequately explain why many reviewers of this novel have discerned its connections to the realistic novel tradition
It would show the ways in which this novel differs from its reputed Anglo-European nineteenth-century models
It would explicate the overarching role of voice in this novel
It would address the ways in which this novel ec hoes the central themes of Hurston’s Their Eyes Are Watching God
It would reveals ways in which these structural features serve to parody novelistic conventions

explanation: 正確答案為 E（It would reveals ways in which these structural features serve to parody novelistic conventions）。末句要求正視突兀的結構，括號說它們可能「intended to undermine traditional Anglo-European novelistic conventions」，即刻意顛覆、戲仿成規。但 B 幾乎逐字對應末句「departs from the traditional models」。

stimulus: The Fourteenth Amendment to the United States Constitut ion, ratified in 1868, prohibits state governments from denying citizens the “equal protection of the laws.” Al though precisely what the framers of the amendment meant by this equal protection clause remains unclear, all interp reters agree that the framers ’ immediate objective was to provide a constitutional warrant for the Civil Rights Act of 1866, which guaranteed the citizenship of all persons born in the United States and subject to United States jurisdiction. This declaration, which was echoed in the text of the Fourteenth Amendment, was designed primarily to counter the Supreme Court’s ruling in Dred Scott v. Sandford that Black people in the United States could be denied citizenship. The act was vetoed by President Andrew Johnson, who argued that the Thirteenth Amendment, which abolished slavery, did not provide Congress with the authority to extend citizenship and equal prot ection to the freed slaves. Although Congress promptly overrode Johnson’s veto, supporters of the act sought to ensure its constitutional foundations with the passage of the Fourteenth Amendment. The broad language of the amendment strongly suggests that its framers were proposing to write into the Constitution not a laundry list of specific civil rights but a principle of equal citizenship that forbids organized society from treating any individual as a member of an inferior class. Yet for the first eight decades of the amendment’s existence, the Supreme Court’s interpretation of the amendment betrayed this ideal of equality. In the Civil Rights Cases of 1883, for example, the Court invented the “state action” limitation, which asserts that “private” decisions by owners of public accommodations and other commercial businesses to segregate their facilities are insulated from the reach of the Fourteenth Amendment’s guarantee of equal protection under the law. After the Second World War, a judicial climate more hospitable to equal protection claims culminated in the Supreme Court’s ruling in Brown v. Bo ard of Education that racially segregated schools violated the equal protection clause of the Fourteenth Amendment. Two doctrines embraced by the Suprem e Court during this period extended the amendment’s reach. First, the Court required es pecially strict scrutiny of legislation that employed a “suspect classification,” meaning discrimination against a group on grounds that could be construed as racial. This doctrine has broadened the application of the Fourteenth Amendment to other, nonracial forms of discrimination, for while some justices have refused to find any legislat ive classification other than race to be constitutionally disfavored, most have been receptive to arguments that at least some nonracial discriminations, sexual discrimination in particular, are “suspect” and deserve this heightened scrutiny by the courts. Second, the Court relaxed the state action limitation on the Fourteenth Amendment, bringing new forms of private conduct within the amendment’s reach.
prompt: Which of the following best describes the main idea of the passage?

options.text: By presenting a list of specific rights, framers of the Fourteenth Amendment were attempting to provide a constitutional basis for broad judicial protection of the principle of equal citizenship.

Only after the Supreme Court adopted the suspect classification approach to reviewing potentially discriminatory legislation was the applicability of the Fourteenth Amendment extended to include sexual discrimination.
Not until after the Second World War did the Supreme Court begin to interpret the Fourteenth Amendment in a manner consistent with the principle of equal citizenship that it expresses.
Interpreters of the Fourteenth Amendment have yet to reach consensus with regard to what its framers meant by the equal protection clause.

Although the reluctance of judges to extend the reach of the Fourteenth Amendment to nonracial discrimination has betrayed the principle of equal ci tizenship, the Supreme Court’s use of the state action limitation to insulate private activity from the amendment’s reach has been more harmful.

explanation: 正確答案為 C（Not until after the Second World War did the Supreme Court begin to interpret the Fourteenth…）。作者說修正案的寬泛文字表達的是平等公民原則，但頭八十年最高法院的解釋「betrayed this ideal」，直到二戰後才出現 Brown 案等符合原則的判決，與 C 相符。A 錯在作者明說制定者寫的「not a laundry list of specific civil rights」。

stimulus: In February 1848 the people of Paris rose in revolt against the constitutional monarchy of Louis-Philippe. In spite of the presence of extraordinary narrative accounts, the Febr uary Days, as this revolt is named, have been greatly ignored by social historians of the last two decades. For each of the three other main insurrections in nineteenth-century Paris—July 1830, June 1848, and May 1871—there exists more than a sketch of participants’ backgrounds and an analysis, more or less rigorous, of th e reasons for the occurrence of the uprisings. Only in the case of the February Revolution do we lack a meaningful illustration of participants that might feature it in the light of what social history has told us about the process of revolutionary mobilization. Two reasons for this relevant neglect seem apparent. First, the insurrection of February has been overshadowed by that of June. The February Revolution reversed a regime, to be sure, but met with so little trouble that it failed to produce any real sense of historical drama. Its successor, on the other hand, seem to pit key socioeconomic groups in a life-or-death struggle and was broadly seen by modern observers as marking a historical departure. Through their interpretations, which impart a constant influence on our understanding of the revolutionary process, the impact of the events of June has been exaggerated, while, as an unintended consequence, the importance of the February insurrection has been diminished. Second, like other “successful” insurrections, the events of February failed to create the most ideal kinds of historical records. Although the June insurrection of 1848 and the Paris Commune of 1871 would be viewed watersheds of nineteenth-century French history by any standard, they also impress the social historian with a signal advantage: these failed insurrections produced a mass of worthwhile documentation as a by-product of authorities’ efforts to search out and punish the rebels. Quite different is the outcome of successful insurrections like those of July 1830 and February 1848. Experiences are retold, but participants typically continue their daily routines without ever recording their activities. Those who served as extraordinary roles may become the objects of highly adorned verbal accounts or in rare cases, of celebratory articles in modern periodicals. And it is true that the publicly acknowledged leaders of an uprising frequently write memoirs. However, such documents are probable to be highly untrustworthy, unrepresentative, and unsystematically conserved, particularly when compared to the detailed judi cial dossiers prepared for everyone arrested following a failed insurrection. As a consequence, it may prove difficult or unlikely to establish for a successful revolution a comprehensive and reliable picture of those who engaged, or to answer even the most basic questions one might pose regarding the social origins of the insurgents.
prompt: It can be assumed from the passage that support for the objectives of the February Revolution was

options.text: negligible

explanation: 正確答案為 E（widespread）。文中說二月革命推翻政權卻「met with so little trouble」，幾乎未遇阻力，連歷史張力都顯不足，可推知其目標獲得廣泛支持。A 與此相反；D 文中未提及革命是否出於自發。

stimulus: The molecules of carbon dioxide in the Earth’s atmosphere influence the heat balance of the Earth by acting as a one-way screen. Although these molecules permit radiation at visible wavelengths, where most of the energy of sunlight is condensed, to pass through, they draw in some of the longer-wavelength, infrared emissions radiated from the Earth’s surface, radiation that would otherwise be sent back into space. For the Earth to preserve a stable average temperature, such emissions fro m the planet must balance incoming solar radiation. If there were no carbon dioxide in the atmosphere, h eat would escape from the Earth much more easily. The surface temperature would be so much lower that the oceans might be a solid mass of ice. Today, however, the implicit problem is too much carbon dioxide. The burning of fossil fuels and the clearing of forests have expanded atmospheric carbon dioxide by about 15 percent in the last hundred years, and we keep up adding carbon dioxide to the atmos phere. Could the increase in carbon dioxide lead to a global rise in average temperature, and could such a rise have serious effects for human society? Mathematical models that allow us to work out the rise in temperature as a function of the increase suggest that the answer is probably yes. Under present conditions a temperature of-18℃ can be observed at an altitude of 5 to 6 kilometers above the Earth. Below this altitude (called the radia ting level), the temperature augments by about 6 ℃ per kilometer approaching the Earth’s surface, where the average temperature is about 15 ℃. An expansion in the amount of carbon dioxide means that there are more molecules of carbon dioxide to absorb infrared radiation. As the capacity of the atmosphere to absorb infrared radiation enlarges, the radiating level and the temperature of the surface must increase. One mathematical model foretells that doubling the atmospheric carbon dioxide would increase the global mean surface temperature by 2.5 ℃. This model assumes that the atmosphere’s comparative humidity remains unchanged and the temperature dec lines with altitude at a rate of 6.5 ℃ per kilometer. The assumption of constant relative humidity is significant , since water vapor in the atmosphere is another effective absorber of radiation at infrared wavelengths. Because warm air can support more moisture than cool air, the relative humidity will be constant only if the am ount of water vapor in the atmosphere enlarges as the temperature expands. Therefore, more infrared radiation wo uld be absorbed and reradiated back to the Earth’s surface. The resultant warming at the surface could be expected to melt snow and ice, decreasing the Earth’s reflectivity. More solar radiation would then be absorbed, causing a further increase in temperature.

demonstrate the usefulness of mathematical models in predicting long-range climatic change

stimulus: The molecules of carbon dioxide in the Earth’s atmosphere influence the heat balance of the Earth by acting as a one-way screen. Although these molecules permit radiation at visible wavelengths, where most of the energy of sunlight is condensed, to pass through, they draw in some of the longer-wavelength, infrared emissions radiated from the Earth’s surface, radiation that would otherwise be sent back into space. For the Earth to preserve a stable average temperature, such emissions fro m the planet must balance incoming solar radiation. If there were no carbon dioxide in the atmosphere, h eat would escape from the Earth much more easily. The surface temperature would be so much lower that the oceans might be a solid mass of ice. Today, however, the implicit problem is too much carbon dioxide. The burning of fossil fuels and the clearing of forests have expanded atmospheric carbon dioxide by about 15 percent in the last hundred years, and we keep up adding carbon dioxide to the atmos phere. Could the increase in carbon dioxide lead to a global rise in average temperature, and could such a rise have serious effects for human society? Mathematical models that allow us to work out the rise in temperature as a function of the increase suggest that the answer is probably yes. Under present conditions a temperature of-18℃ can be observed at an altitude of 5 to 6 kilometers above the Earth. Below this altitude (called the radia ting level), the temperature augments by about 6 ℃ per kilometer approaching the Earth’s surface, where the average temperature is about 15 ℃. An expansion in the amount of carbon dioxide means that there are more molecules of carbon dioxide to absorb infrared radiation. As the capacity of the atmosphere to absorb infrared radiation enlarges, the radiating level and the temperature of the surface must increase. One mathematical model foretells that doubling the atmospheric carbon dioxide would increase the global mean surface temperature by 2.5 ℃. This model assumes that the atmosphere’s comparative humidity remains unchanged and the temperature dec lines with altitude at a rate of 6.5 ℃ per kilometer. The assumption of constant relative humidity is significant , since water vapor in the atmosphere is another effective absorber of radiation at infrared wavelengths. Because warm air can support more moisture than cool air, the relative humidity will be constant only if the am ount of water vapor in the atmosphere enlarges as the temperature expands. Therefore, more infrared radiation wo uld be absorbed and reradiated back to the Earth’s surface. The resultant warming at the surface could be expected to melt snow and ice, decreasing the Earth’s reflectivity. More solar radiation would then be absorbed, causing a further increase in temperature.

stimulus: All of Francoise Duparc’s surviving paintings mix portraiture and genre. Her subjects appear to be acquaintances whom she has asked to pose; she has reaped both their self-consciousness and the spontaneity of their everyday activities, the description of which distinguishes genre painting. stimulus: Before Laura Gilpin (1891-1979), few women in the hist ory of photography had so committed themselves to chronicling the landscape. Other women had photographe d the land, but none can be treated as a landscape photographer with a continued body of work recording the physical terrain. Anne Brigman often photographed woodlands and coastal areas, but they were mostly se ttings for her craftily placed subjects. Dorothea Lange’s landscapes were always thought of as equivalent to her images of rural women. At the same time that Gilpin’s interest in land scape work differentiated her from most other women photographers, her approach to landscape photography set her apart from men photographers who, like Gilpin, recorded the western United States. Western American landscape photography grew out of a male tradition, initiated by photographers attached to government and me rcantile survey teams that went west in the 1860’s and 1870’s. These explorer-photographers documented the West that their employers wanted to see: a outlandish and graceful land shaped by miraculous natural forces, unpopulated and ready for American settlement. The next generation of male photographers, ch aracterized by Ansel Adams and Eliot Porter, often worked with conservationist groups rather than gove rnment agencies or commercial companies, but they nonetheless conserved the “heroic” style and preserved th e role of deferential outsider peering in with reverence at a delicate natural world. For Gilpin, by contrast, the landscape was neither an empty vista awaiting human settlement nor a jewel-like scene opposing human intrusion, but a artificial landscape with a affluent history and tradition of its own, an environment that formed and molded the lives of its residents. Her photographs of the Rio Grande, for example, coherently describe the river in terms of its importance to human culture: as a source of irrigation water, a source of food for livestock, and a supplier of town sites. Also educative is Gilpin’s general avoidance of excessive close-ups of her natural subjects: for her, symbolic details could never indicate the intricacies of the interrelationship between people an d nature that made the landscape a persuasive subject. While it is perilous to draw conclusions about a “feminine” way of seeing from the work of one woman, it can nonetheless be maintained that Gilpin’s unusual approach to landscape photography was similar to the work of many women writers who, far more than their male counterparts, depicted the landscape in terms of its potential to nurture human life. stimulus: The social sciences are less likely than other rational enterprises to get credit for their achievements. Arguably, this is so because the theories and conc eptual constructs of the social sciences are especially available: human intelligence seized truths about human affairs with speci al facility. And the discoveri es of the soci al sciences, once quarantined and marked, are quickly absorbed into ordinary wisdom, whereupon they lose their distinctiveness as scientific advances. stimulus: The 1960’s witnessed two complete social movement s: the civil rights movement and the movement protesting the war in Vietnam. Even though they overlappe d in time, they were largely disparate. For a brief moment in 1967, however, it appeared that the two m ovements might coalesce under the leadership of Martin Luther King, Jr. King’s part in the antiwar movement appears to require little explanation, because he was the foremost advocate of nonviolence of his time. stimulus: National character is not formally studied by social scientists in discussing econom ic and social development nowadays. stimulus: Comparing designs in music with visual designs gives rise to involving questions. We are familiar with the effortless transfers of terms denoting qualities from one field to another. The fundamental problem can be put this way: can music sound the way a design looks? The components of music are not the same as those of painting. Two facts about the relationship between broad featur es of a work and their pe rceptual conditions must be kept distinct. First, the worldwide features of a visual or auditory complex are determined by the perceptible parts and their relations. Thus, any striking change in the parts or their relations makes a change in some of the worldwide feature. Second, a change in the parts or their relations may leave other worldwide features unchanged.

options.text: comparisons are not equations

questions concerning perception are psychological

stimulus: Visual recognition includes storing and retrieving memories. Neural activity, triggered by the eye, forms an image in the brain’s memory system that consists of an internal representation of the viewed object. When an object is encountered again, it is corresponded with its internal representation and thereby discerned. Dispute surrounds the question of whether recognition is a parallel, one-step procedure or a serial, step-by-step one. Psychologists of the Gestalt school assert that objects are recognized as wholes in a parallel process: the internal representation is corresponded with the retinal image in a single operation. Other psychologists have proposed that internal representation characteristics are corresponded serially with an object’s characteristics. Although some experiments show that, as an object becomes familiar, its internal representation becomes more holistic and the recognition pro cedure equivalently more parallel, the weight of evidence seems to support the serial hypothesis, at least for objects that are not particularly simple and familiar.
prompt: The author is primarily concerned with

options.text: explaining how the brain receives images
synthesizing hypotheses of visual recognition
examining the evidence supporting the serial recognition hypothesis
discussing visual recognition and some hypotheses proposed to explain it
reporting on recent experiments dealing with me mory systems and their relationship to neural activity

explanation: 正確答案為 D（discussing visual recognition and some hypotheses proposed to explain it）。全文先說明視覺辨識的機制（儲存與提取記憶、與內部表徵比對），再介紹 Gestalt 的平行假說與序列假說的爭論，即討論視覺辨識及其解釋假說。C 只是末句的結論；B 的 synthesizing 不符，作者未整合兩者。

stimulus: An enigmatic phenomenon is the ability of over-water migr ants to travel on course. Birds, bees, and other species can keep track of time w ithout any sensitive cues from the outsi de world, and such “biological clocks”are definitely due to their “compass sense.” For in stance, they can utilize the position of the Sun or stars, along with the time of day, to find north. stimulus: Mycorrhizal fungi contaminate more plants than do any other fungi and are important for many plants to flourish, but they have escaped extensive investigati on until recently for two reasons. First, the symbiotic association is so well-balanced that the roots of host plan ts show no harm even when densely infected. Second, the fungi cannot as yet be developed in the absence of a living root. Despite these di fficulties, there has been significant new work that indicates that this symbiotic association can be used to achieve more inexpensive use of costly superphosphate fertilizer and to allow better exploitation of cheaper, less soluble rock phosphate. Mycorrhizal benefits are not confined to improved phos phate uptake in host plants. In legumes, mycorrhizal inoculation has expanded nitrogen fi xation beyond levels achieved by joining phosphate fertilizer alone. Certain symbiotic associations also promote the host plan t’s resistance to detrimental root fungi. Whether this resistance results from exclusion of destructive fungi through competition for sites, from metabolic change involving antibiotic production, or from increased vigor is inconclusive.
prompt: Which of the following most accurately describes the passage?

options.text: A description of a replicable experiment
A summary report of new findings
A recommendation for abandoning a difficult area of research
A refutation of an earlier hypothesis
A confirmation of earlier research

explanation: 正確答案為 B（A summary report of new findings）。文章先說明菌根真菌過去少被研究的兩個原因，接著以「significant new work」介紹其節省磷肥、提升固氮與抗病等新發現，屬新發現的摘要報告。A 文中並未描述可重複的實驗步驟；D、E 也沒有反駁或確認先前研究。

stimulus: Flatfish, such as the flounder, are among the few vertebra tes that lack relative bilateral symmetry (symmetry in which structures to the left and right of the body’s midline are mirror images). Most striking among the many asymmetries evident in an adult flatfish is eye placement: before maturity one eye moves, so that in an adult flatfish both eyes are on the same side of the head. While in most species with asymmetries nearly all adults share the same asymmetry, members of the starry flounder species can be either left-eyed (both eyes on the left side of head) or right-eyed. In the waters between the United States and Japan, the starry flounder populations vary from about 50 percent left-eyed off th e United States West Coast, through about 70 percent left-eyed halfway between the United States and Japan, to nearly 100 percent left-eyed off the Japanese coast. Biologists call this kind of gradual change over a fixed geographic range a “cline” and explain clines as strong clues that the variation is adaptive, a response to environmental discrepancies. For the starry flounder this interpretation suggests that a geometric difference (between fish that are mirror images of one another) is adaptive, that left-eyedness in the Japanese starry flounder has been selected for, which causes a complex question: what is the selective advantage in having both eyes on one side rather than on the other? The ease with which a fish can reverse the influence of the sidedness of its eye asymmetry simply by turning around has made biologists st udy internal anatomy, especially the optic nerves, for the answer. In all flatfish the optic nerves cross, so that the right optic nerve is joined to the brain’s left side and vice versa. This crossing leads to an asymmetry, as one optic nerve must cross above or below the other. G. H. Parker reasoned that if, for instance, a flatfish’s left eye moved wh en the right optic nerve was on top, there would be a wresting of nerves, which might be automatically unf avorable. For starry flounders, then, the left-eyed diversity would be selected against, since in a starry flounder the left optic nerve is dominant. The problem with the above interpretation is that the Japanese starry flounder population is almost merely left-eyed, a natural selecti on never contributes to a purely less beneficial variation. As other interpretations proved evenly unreasonable, biologists concluded that there is no necessary adaptive difference between left-eyedness and right-eyedness, and that the two properties are genetically related to some other adaptively important characteristic. This situation is on e frequently met by evolutionary biologists, who must often determine whether a characteristic is adaptive or sel ectively neutral. As for the left-eyed and right-eyed flatfish, their difference, however evident, appears to be an evolutionary red herring.

options.text: are not basically bilaterally symmetric

have both eyes on the same side of the head
tend to cluster in only certain geographic regions

explanation: 正確答案為 C（do not all share the same asymmetry）。第一段說「in most species with asymmetries nearly all adults share the same asymmetry」，而 starry flounder 可能左眼型或右眼型。A、D 是所有比目魚的共同特徵，不能區分；B 眼睛在成熟前移動也是一般比目魚的情形。
